data.name: Navansh
data.gender_notes: Navansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: New Life, Birth of New Era
data.long_meaning: Navansh is a name derived from Sanskrit roots meaning 'new' (nav) and 'life' (ansh). This name symbolizes the beginning of a new life, a new era, or a new cycle. In Hindu mythology, Navansh is associated with the god Brahma, the creator of the universe, representing the endless cycle of birth, life, and death. The name Navansh carries the meaning “New Life, Birth of New Era” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Navansh usually hope their child will grow to embody new life, birth of new era and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name imbued with the energy of new beginnings and the power to create.
data.etymology: Navansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “New Life, Birth of New Era.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Navansh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Navansh is a unique and powerful name rooted in Indian culture and language. It reflects the values of renewal and regeneration, which are significant aspects of Hinduism. The name is often given to newborns evoking the hope of a promising and prosperous future.
data.spiritual_significance: Navansh is a name that carries deep spiritual significance and resonates with the Hindu idea of the cyclic nature of life. It serves as a constant reminder of the eternal cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, encouraging the individual to live in the present while striving for spiritual growth and enlightenment. The name connects the bearer to the roots of Hinduism and reinforces the belief in the profound cyclic nature of the universe.

historical_references.reference: Navansh is a Sanskrit term that translates to 'nine forms'. It is a name given to the nine avatars of the Hindu deity Vishnu. These nine avatars are believed to have appeared in the world in different historical periods to protect the dharma (righteous order) and maintain balance in the universe.

historical_references.reference: Navansh is also the name of a medieval Hindu kingdom located in present-day Gujarat, India. It was founded by the Jadeja Rajputs in the 11th century AD and existed until the 16th century AD. The kingdom was known for its rich culture and trade with other regions, particularly Arab and Persian markets.
